item.title: Sparse-data method estimates sea surface temperatures 40% more accurately than conventional approach
item.description: Researchers have developed a method for extrapolating sea surface temperatures from sparse data that is significantly more accurate than other commonly used computational methods and slightly more accurate than the best-performing AI model, while taking a fraction of the time to train. The work has implications for both short-term weather forecasting and longer-term climate predictions. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Portugal's Pinhal Interior shows why fire and floods are part of the same cycle
item.description: Across southern Europe, increasingly extreme heat, wildfire and intense rainfall are forcing planners to consider how one event can alter the risk of the next. Portugal's exceptionally wet winter and another summer of wildfire risk are an example of this. As a professor of architecture and climate change adaptation who has been following the cyclical nature of weather extremes in the Pinhal Interior region since the deadly 2017 fires, I explain why prevention must connect forests, settlements, slopes and waterways. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Extremely massive galaxy proto-supercluster smashes distance record
item.description: An international team of astronomers has discovered the most distant progenitor to a galaxy supercluster ever. The discovery supports existing theories of how galaxy clusters evolve and reveals how they are connected to the larger cosmic web. The study relies largely on data from the ODIN survey, conducted with the U.S. Department of Energy-fabricated Dark Energy Camera on the U.S. National Science Foundation Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope in Chile. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Optimizing tomato plant growth with microbes
item.description: Plants are home to a diverse array of microorganisms that support their growth and help them adapt to environmental stress—of which there has been an abundance lately. High temperatures and drought caused by human-induced climate change have led to reduced crop yields and the use of biofertilizers such as rhizosphere microorganisms, which help plants absorb nutrients and increase their resistance to disease and stress. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 13 mil reproducciones · 189 reacciones | Grande susto - Um entregador mexicano conseguiu evitar uma tragédia em uma avenida da cidade de Puebla. Luís Henrique Cruz, funcionário de uma rede de supermercados da cidade, salvou uma menina de 3 anos de ser atropelada no local, em um ato heróico. ➡️ O caso ocorreu no domingo (6) na cidade de Puebla, no México, e foi registrado por uma câmera de segurança do supermercado. Cruz trabalhava em um carregamento na porta do estabelecimento quando percebeu a menina correndo perto da avenida. Ele chegou a caminhar em direção à criança, mas desistiu ao ver a mãe dela se aproximando. Nesse momento, no entanto, a menina disparou em direção à avenida movimentada. A mãe tentou pegá-la, mas acabou caindo, e Cruz, então se jogou no meio da rua. Ele fez sinal para os carros pararem e conseguiu agarrar a menina a centímetros de um dos veículos, que também parou ao avistar a criança. Por causa do ato heróico, Cruz recebeu um cheque de cerca de R$ 6 mil do supermercado em que trabalha.
